prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1286; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the claimant's vehicle, and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver involved is named on the policy and that the policy was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the claim. They confirm several details of the scene and the vehicle, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the impact.

Entry 4: Police records and the statements gathered at the scene confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 5: The vehicle damage is consistent with the impact described by both parties. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history provided.

Entry 6: The claimant has reported a wrist fracture. The injury fits the type and force of the collision, and no earlier injury to the same area is known from medical history or prior claims.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's account through counsel. The account has remained the same in every conversation so far, with no changes in the sequence of events.

Entry 8: Medical records show treatment followed a typical course for this kind of fracture, with care tapering as the claimant's condition improved. Requested updated records from the treating provider.

Entry 9: File remains open pending the outstanding medical records and the attorney's demand package. Reserves will be reviewed once those documents are received.
